open_points.subject: Viewer entry rate limiting
open_points.question: What limit applies to viewer entry, what identifies the rate-limit bucket, which attempts consume it, and what observable response and recovery time follow when it is exceeded?
options: Limit by access credential or viewer
Limit by both source address and credential
open_points.default_guess: Use separate source-address and credential buckets, count failed attempts, and return a concealed rate-limit response with a retry interval.

witness.initial: A valid viewer access link exists and has not been revoked.
events: An attacker submits repeated invalid access secrets from the same address.
The legitimate viewer then submits the valid link from that address.
outcomes: An address-based limit refuses the legitimate viewer until the window expires.
A credential-based limit admits the legitimate viewer because the invalid attempts used another bucket.
witness.observer: The legitimate viewer and the portal operator

open_points.subject: Actors and authorization for progress-read budget creation
open_points.text: “reading the progress of a project that has no budget yet creates its empty manual budget version, also for an archived project” versus “all viewer capabilities are read-only; a viewer can never mutate data”
open_points.question: Which progress-reading actors and operations trigger the creation, and is the side effect authorized solely by the progress-read capability or does it require a budget-mutation capability?
options: Every authorized progress read triggers it, including a viewer read
Only a staff progress read triggers it
Every read may trigger a system-owned side effect that is not treated as a viewer mutation
open_points.default_guess: Every authorized progress read triggers one system-owned initialization using the read authorization, while the audit records the requesting principal.

witness.initial: An archived project has an active viewer grant and no budget.
events: The viewer enters through a valid access link.
The viewer requests the project's progress.
outcomes: The request succeeds and creates an empty manual budget, so the viewer's read changes stored project data.
The read-only viewer rule prevents the creation, leaving the project without a budget or causing the request to be refused.
witness.observer: The viewer immediately, and staff on a later budget read

open_points.subject: State of the automatically created manual budget version
open_points.question: Is the created version active or inactive, what source/version identity does it receive, and what budget and progress state is observable immediately after creation?
options: Create and activate an empty manual budget version
Create an inactive manual budget version
Create an initialization record that is not yet a selectable budget version
open_points.default_guess: Create and activate one empty manual budget version with a portal-assigned identity.

witness.initial: An archived project has no budget or progress records.
events: An authorized principal reads its progress.
The same principal then reads the budget summary.
outcomes: The new manual version is active and the budget summary reports a manual budget with no sections.
The new version is inactive, so the budget summary still reports budget data as unavailable.

open_points.subject: Empty budget versus unavailable-data invariant
open_points.text: “the one exception is the empty manual budget of R0-24” versus “Unavailable data is shown explicitly, never fabricated or replaced by silent zeros” and “missing data is explicit, never guessed, zeroed, or clamped”
open_points.question: After a progress read initializes the empty manual budget, must client-facing reads present a real zero-valued manual budget or continue to present the absent planned budget and progress as unavailable?
options: Expose the initialized manual budget with zero totals
Expose the stored version but mark its financial and progress values unavailable
Keep the initialization invisible until staff supplies planned sections
open_points.default_guess: Expose the manual source and empty section list, but mark derived financial and progress values unavailable rather than reporting zero.

witness.initial: An archived, viewer-granted project has no budget.
events: A viewer reads progress, causing the R0-24 initialization.
The viewer opens the budget summary.
outcomes: The viewer sees a manual budget whose totals are zero because its section list is empty.
The viewer sees budget and derived values as unavailable because no planned amounts exist.

open_points.subject: Failure of the progress-read initialization side effect
open_points.text: “reading the progress of a project that has no budget yet creates its empty manual budget version”
open_points.question: What happens when progress is readable but the empty manual budget cannot be persisted: does the read fail, return progress without creating the budget, or succeed with an unavailable result, and what is audited?
options: Fail the entire progress read with a storage error and create nothing
Return the readable progress while leaving the budget absent
Return an unavailable progress result and retry initialization on a later read
open_points.default_guess: Fail the entire operation atomically with a storage-unavailable error and persist neither the budget nor its audit record.

witness.initial: An authorized principal can read an archived project with no budget, but storage rejects the budget insertion.
outcomes: The progress request fails because its required initialization could not complete.
The progress request succeeds as a read while the project remains without a budget.

open_points.subject: Concurrent initialization of the empty manual budget
open_points.question: When multiple progress reads concurrently observe that no budget exists, what invariant prevents duplicate manual versions, and do all successful reads resolve to the same version?
options: Atomically create exactly one version and have all reads use it
Allow multiple empty versions but activate only one
Let one request succeed and fail competing reads with a conflict
open_points.default_guess: Atomically create at most one empty manual version per project and have concurrent reads resolve to that same version.

witness.initial: An archived project has no budget and two authorized sessions can read it.
events: Viewer B requests progress concurrently before A's insertion is visible.
outcomes: Exactly one empty manual version is stored and both reads resolve to it.
Two empty manual versions are stored, or one reader receives a conflict that the other does not.
witness.observer: The two readers and an administrator inspecting the project's budget history
